title: BSV.place — Corrections and evidence briefs
description: Material revisions and evidence-first responses to common BSV objections.

items.title: Canonical objection corpus expanded · v1.1.0
items.content_text: Split the original eight combined briefs into twenty-eight canonical objection families, added risk and review metadata, claim-level source mappings, evidence gaps, and explicit falsifiability.

items.title: Current TypeScript sources corrected · v1.0.1
items.content_text: Updated the implementation desk to use the current bsv-blockchain/ts-stack monorepo and labeled archived predecessor repositories and maintainer catalogs appropriately.

items.title: BSV.place launched · v1.0.0
items.content_text: Published the initial evidence desk with eight briefs, an editorial method, and primary-source resource desk.

items.title: Public corrections and revision history opened
items.content_text: Added structured correction and missing-objection intake, a public revision log, and an explicit promise to preserve material changes.

items.title: Independent static publication established
items.content_text: The durable editorial source now publishes a generated static artifact to GitHub Pages with a protected custom domain and enforced HTTPS.

items.title: Does the BSV case depend on Craig Wright being Satoshi?
items.content_text: No identity claim is required. Software, network rules, economics, and actual use should stand or fall on inspectable evidence of their own.

items.title: What did the COPA judgment establish—and what does it not decide?
items.content_text: The judgment is an essential legal record about Craig Wright's identity claim. It is not a test report for every protocol or application claim.

items.title: Is BSV captured by a small set of institutions and patrons?
items.content_text: Concentration is a legitimate dependency question. It should be answered with an inventory of authority, funding, code ownership, operators, and replaceability—not a decentralization slogan.

items.title: How should a serious person respond to the “scam” or “cult” label?
items.content_text: A label is not a technical analysis, but it often points to a valid proof problem: were people sold allegiance and price stories instead of working utility and disclosed risk?

items.title: Where are the users?
items.content_text: The public adoption proof remains thinner than the technical inventory. That gap should be measured, not covered with anecdotes or raw transaction counts.

items.title: Does anything economically need BSV?
items.content_text: Correct: a cheap transaction is a component, not a product. The case must be a workflow where public proofs, tiny payments, or portable signed records change user value or unit economics.

items.title: Does building on BSV create unacceptable reputational risk?
items.content_text: That is a real commercial risk affecting hiring, partnerships, fundraising, and distribution. It can be reduced by clean-room product framing and evidence, not denied.

items.title: Is BSV “really Bitcoin”?
items.content_text: Chain identity is partly historical and social. For a product decision, compare implemented design goals and current rules instead of demanding agreement on a purity title.

items.title: Is “Satoshi's Vision” a defensible description?
items.content_text: The phrase is defensible only when defined narrowly as a set of design goals. It should not imply that every current governance choice appears in, or is compelled by, the whitepaper.

items.title: Can nodes reject a longer proof-of-work chain and still claim Bitcoin rules?
items.content_text: This is a serious protocol-governance dispute. Proof of work coordinates valid history; the hard questions are who defines validity, what policies can change it, and how operators learn the rules.

items.title: Can BSV freeze or reassign coins?
items.content_text: The published governance surface is real and consequential. It should be evaluated as a disputed-property recovery tradeoff—not denied or confused with ordinary wallet authority.

items.title: What if a court or claimant gets asset recovery wrong?
items.content_text: Correct. Legal process is a risk-control system, not an oracle. The relevant mitigations are narrow scope, notice, challenge, appeal, transparency, liability, and technical reversibility.

items.title: Does the BSV Association function as a central authority?
items.content_text: BSV does include explicit institutional governance. The defensible question is whether its scope, checks, transparency, and fit are acceptable for a use case.

items.title: Is the Open BSV License actually open—and can builders exit?
items.content_text: The rail-use condition is a material dependency. Inventory licenses component by component; do not use “open source” as a blanket shorthand.

items.title: Do delistings and weak liquidity make BSV unusable?
items.content_text: Liquidity and service access are real operational dependencies for some products and nearly incidental for others. They must be tested at decision time.

items.title: Do price and “flippening” narratives invalidate the builder case?
items.content_text: They do not invalidate a working product, but they contaminate its credibility and attract the wrong success metrics.

items.title: Why does BSV discourse so often feel tribal or abusive?
items.content_text: Factional tone is a real credibility and distribution cost. Friendly hostility does not become helpful because it comes from an ally.

items.title: What can a skeptical person actually try?
items.content_text: That request is an opportunity. Every capability claim should lead to a bounded, reproducible path with expected output and honest failure handling.

items.title: Is BSV too complicated to build on?
items.content_text: The cognitive-load objection is valid. A newcomer should start with one user outcome and a high-level API, then reveal lower layers only when they solve a real problem.

items.title: Is BRC-100 real interoperability or one vendor's interface?
items.content_text: That is the right proof standard. BRC-100 is a substantial public interface; interoperability depends on conforming independent implementations and observable compatibility.

items.title: Can users actually leave a wallet, app, or overlay?
items.content_text: Correct. Portability is an operational property demonstrated by export, import, discovery, replacement, and recovery—not inferred from public keys or blockchain storage.

items.title: Is BSV scaling real, or a datacenter marketing claim?
items.content_text: BSV has a coherent large-block architecture and public Teranode source. Capacity, independent reproduction, production behavior, demand, and operator diversity remain separate claims.

items.title: What do hashpower and reorganization history mean for BSV security?
items.content_text: Hash economics, transaction validity, confirmation policy, topology, monitoring, and governance response are separate security layers. None should be hand-waved.

items.title: Do DAR or compliance controls change BSV's legal classification?
items.content_text: Mechanisms can affect a legal analysis, but a slogan cannot supply one. Classification is jurisdiction-, fact-, transaction-, and time-specific and requires counsel.

items.title: Why have so many funded BSV projects disappeared?
items.content_text: Failed projects are normal; missing accountability is not. Judge a current ecosystem by maintained products, user outcomes, and transparent status—not by cumulative launch announcements.

items.title: Is BSV just a cheap database for spam?
items.content_text: This is a genuine design-priority disagreement. Cheap public blockspace can support proofs and signed records while imposing permanent-resource and privacy costs.

items.title: Can miners, the chain, or an app sign as me or read my private data?
items.content_text: These are different authority layers. Network recovery can affect accepted coin ownership without automatically granting a user's signing keys, decryption keys, certificates, or app permissions.

items.title: Does Project Babbage depend too heavily on the BSV rail?
items.content_text: BSV is the current rail, so failure is a material dependency. Portability claims must distinguish reusable interfaces and user data from BSV-specific transactions, proofs, licenses, and services.
